title: TTFT oscillation from mixed-kernel handshake under heterogeneous session lengths
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Multiple customers (one Dedicated customer reporting SLA breaches and several Hosted customers showing intermittent spikes) observed large TTFT oscillations and tokens/sec degradation during short-session multiplexed workloads. The behavior started after kernel selector heuristics were relaxed in runtime-1.22 to prefer smaller-footprint INT8 kernels for memory-constrained workers. This ticket coordinates the urgent investigation, customer communication, and rollout of a short-term stabilizing patch plus a safer long-term selector change.
impact_summary: Observed impact: TTFT spikes from 30-300ms baseline up to +600ms for first token on 8/16 GPU pools under mixed short/long prompt workloads. Throughput for burst sessions dropped 25-40% in multiplexed queues. One Dedicated customer (Acme Analytics) reported three SLA violations in the last 48h and opened an escalation. A handful of Hosted customers saw degraded 95th and 99th percentile latency on small-context routes.
reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy model variant with mixed-precision INT8 kernels enabled on worker pool with heterogeneous sequence-length traffic
2) Run multiplexed short-session traffic (prompt length ~8 tokens, avg response 40 tokens) concurrently with occasional long requests (prompt length >1024)
3) Observe kernel handshake path that switches from int8 fast path to fallback kernels when a long request arrives, causing concurrent memcpy and KV cache flush racing the next short-session first-token path
4) Measure TTFT and tokens/sec at multiplexing ratios 90:10 short:long and 70:30, both show TTFT oscillations and throughput sag
investigation_findings:
- Kernel selector heuristics chose INT8 kernels for small-memory workers; those kernels assume contiguous KV layouts and use an accelerated memcpy path.
- When long-context requests arrive they trigger a fallback to a different kernel that performs an in-place KV rebase; the worker concurrently services enqueued short-session streams which hit a transient state requiring KV cache snapshot/restore.
- The code paths currently synchronize via a coarse global worker mutex leading to head-of-line blocking for prioritised short sessions.
- The probability of the pathological handshake increases non-linearly with multiplexing and with models using grouped attention blocks (seen on two community-verified models and an internal tuned Llama variant).
root_cause_summary: A mismatch between the relaxed kernel-selection policy (favoring low-memory int8 kernels) and the worker's KV cache layout transitions for long-context requests caused expensive snapshot/restore work and mutex-held operations that delayed first-token generation for enqueued short streams. The regression surfaced under high-multiplex short-session loads and mixed model architectures.
short_term_mitigation:
1) Roll back the kernel selector change for affected worker pools (hotpatch to runtime-1.22: enforce per-worker kernel compatibility checks)
2) Apply a per-customer temporary concurrency floor for dedicated tenants to prevent extreme multiplex ratios for 24-72h
3) Deploy a targeted worker config that pins a conservative kernel set for mixed-length workloads (configuration flag runtime.pin_kernel_set=true)
4) Notify impacted customers with remediation ETA and offer Dedicated customers prioritized warmstart credits and SLA credit calculations
long_term_plan:
1) Implement fine-grained kernel compatibility metadata so selector prefers kernels that are safe under KV rebase scenarios rather than purely memory footprint; add tests for mixed-length multiplexing.
2) Replace global worker mutex with a split lock around KV snapshot/restore to reduce head-of-line blocking.
3) Add automated chaos tests that simulate long-request-induced kernel transitions during heavy multiplexing and run in CI gating.
4) Add console alerting for multiplex ratio shifts and automatic per-pool kernel policy rollbacks when TTFT slope exceeds threshold.
technical_decisions: Temporary rollback of heuristic change in runtime-1.22 for affected pools
Introduce kernel capability metadata field (capabilities:list) and selector whitelist policy
Prefer split-lock design for KV cache snapshot path to minimize blocking on first-token critical path
